answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 14 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The lotus multiplier is published, charged in pulse, and basalt lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3970 identities would post 1371 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
